audit_status.source_base: Hebrew Numbers / Bemidbar rebellion, intercession, wilderness-judgment, and failed-invasion text tradition, draft aligned later
audit_status.review_note: First-pass draft reviewed for communal panic, return-to-Egypt proposal, Joshua and Caleb's appeal, Moses' intercession, Divine pardon and judgment, forty-year wilderness consequence, scout deaths, and presumptuous invasion. Strong anti-trauma, anti-abuse, anti-colonial, and anti-militarization safeguards required.

verses.restored: All congregation lifted up and gave their voice, and people wept that night.

familiar.text: And all the congregation lifted up their voice, and cried; and the people wept that night.

modern.text: Then the whole congregation lifted up their voices and cried out, and that night the people wept.

original.text: וַתִּשָּׂא֙ כָּל הָ֣עֵדָ֔ה וַֽיִּתְּנ֖וּ אֶת קוֹלָ֑ם וַיִּבְכּ֥וּ הָעָ֖ם בַּלַּ֥יְלָה הַהֽוּא

verses.restored: All children of Israel murmured against Moses and Aaron; whole congregation said to them, Would that we had died in land of Egypt, or would that in this wilderness we had died!

familiar.text: And all the children of Israel murmured against Moses and against Aaron: and the whole congregation said unto them, Would God that we had died in the land of Egypt! or would God we had died in this wilderness!

modern.text: All the Israelites grumbled against Moses and Aaron, and the whole congregation said to them, “If only we had died in the land of Egypt, or if only we had died in this wilderness!

original.text: וַיִּלֹּ֨נוּ֙ עַל מֹשֶׁ֣ה וְעַֽל אַהֲרֹ֔ן כֹּ֖ל בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וַֽיֹּאמְר֨וּ אֲלֵהֶ֜ם כָּל הָעֵדָ֗ה לוּ מַ֨תְנוּ֙ בְּאֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרַ֔יִם א֛וֹ בַּמִּדְבָּ֥ר הַזֶּ֖ה לוּ מָֽתְנוּ

verses.restored: Why is YHWH bringing us to this land to fall by sword? Our wives and our little ones will become plunder. Would it not be good for us to return to Egypt?

familiar.text: And wherefore hath the LORD brought us unto this land, to fall by the sword, that our wives and our children should be a prey? were it not better for us to return into Egypt?

modern.text: Why is the LORD bringing us into this land to fall by the sword? Our wives and children will become plunder. Would it not be better for us to go back to Egypt?”

original.text: וְלָמָ֣ה יְ֠הוָה מֵבִ֨יא אֹתָ֜נוּ אֶל הָאָ֤רֶץ הַזֹּאת֙ לִנְפֹּ֣ל בַּחֶ֔רֶב נָשֵׁ֥ינוּ וְטַפֵּ֖נוּ יִהְי֣וּ לָבַ֑ז הֲל֧וֹא ט֦וֹב לָ֖נוּ שׁ֥וּב מִצְרָֽיְמָה

verses.restored: They said one to another, Let us appoint a head and return to Egypt.

familiar.text: And they said one to another, Let us make a captain, and let us return into Egypt.

modern.text: So they said to one another, “Let us appoint a leader and return to Egypt.”

original.text: וַיֹּאמְר֖וּ אִ֣ישׁ אֶל אָחִ֑יו נִתְּנָ֥ה רֹ֖אשׁ וְנָשׁ֥וּבָה מִצְרָֽיְמָה

verses.restored: Moses and Aaron fell upon their faces before all assembly of congregation of children of Israel.

familiar.text: Then Moses and Aaron fell on their faces before all the assembly of the congregation of the children of Israel.

modern.text: Then Moses and Aaron fell facedown before the whole assembly of the congregation of Israel.

original.text: וַיִּפֹּ֥ל מֹשֶׁ֛ה וְאַהֲרֹ֖ן עַל פְּנֵיהֶ֑ם לִפְנֵ֕י כָּל קְהַ֥ל עֲדַ֖ת בְּנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל

verses.restored: Joshua son of Nun and Caleb son of Jephunneh, from those who scouted land, tore their garments.

familiar.text: And Joshua the son of Nun, and Caleb the son of Jephunneh, which were of them that searched the land, rent their clothes:

modern.text: Joshua son of Nun and Caleb son of Jephunneh, who were among those who had spied out the land, tore their clothes

original.text: וִיהוֹשֻׁ֣עַ בִּן נ֗וּן וְכָלֵב֙ בֶּן יְפֻנֶּ֔ה מִן הַתָּרִ֖ים אֶת הָאָ֑רֶץ קָרְע֖וּ בִּגְדֵיהֶֽם

familiar.text: And they spake unto all the company of the children of Israel, saying, The land, which we passed through to search it, is an exceeding good land.

modern.text: and said to the whole congregation of Israel, “The land we passed through and explored is an exceedingly good land.

original.text: וַיֹּ֣אמְר֔וּ אֶל כָּל עֲדַ֥ת בְּנֵֽי יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל לֵאמֹ֑ר הָאָ֗רֶץ אֲשֶׁ֨ר עָבַ֤רְנוּ בָהּ֙ לָת֣וּר אֹתָ֔הּ טוֹבָ֥ה הָאָ֖רֶץ מְאֹ֥ד מְאֹֽד

verses.restored: If YHWH delights in us, he will bring us into this land and give it to us, a land flowing with milk and honey.

familiar.text: If the LORD delight in us, then he will bring us into this land, and give it us; a land which floweth with milk and honey.

modern.text: If the LORD delights in us, He will bring us into this land, a land flowing with milk and honey, and He will give it to us.

original.text: אִם חָפֵ֥ץ בָּ֨נוּ֙ יְהוָ֔ה וְהֵבִ֤יא אֹתָ֨נוּ֙ אֶל הָאָ֣רֶץ הַזֹּ֔את וּנְתָנָ֖הּ לָ֑נוּ אֶ֕רֶץ אֲשֶׁר הִ֛וא זָבַ֥ת חָלָ֖ב וּדְבָֽשׁ

verses.restored: Only do not rebel against YHWH, and you, do not fear people of land, for they are our bread; their shade/protection has turned aside from them, and YHWH is with us. Do not fear them.

familiar.text: Only rebel not ye against the LORD, neither fear ye the people of the land; for they are bread for us: their defence is departed from them, and the LORD is with us: fear them not.

modern.text: Only do not rebel against the LORD, and do not be afraid of the people of the land, for they will be like bread for us. Their protection has been removed, and the LORD is with us. Do not be afraid of them!”

original.text: אַ֣ךְ בַּֽיהוָה֮ אַל תִּמְרֹדוּ֒ וְאַתֶּ֗ם אַל תִּֽירְאוּ֙ אֶת עַ֣ם הָאָ֔רֶץ כִּ֥י לַחְמֵ֖נוּ הֵ֑ם סָ֣ר צִלָּ֧ם מֵעֲלֵיהֶ֛ם וַֽיהוָ֥ה אִתָּ֖נוּ אַל תִּירָאֻֽם

verses.restored: All congregation said to stone them with stones. Then glory of YHWH appeared in tent of meeting to all children of Israel.

familiar.text: But all the congregation bade stone them with stones. And the glory of the LORD appeared in the tabernacle of the congregation before all the children of Israel.

modern.text: But the whole congregation threatened to stone Joshua and Caleb. Then the glory of the LORD appeared to all the Israelites at the Tent of Meeting.

original.text: וַיֹּֽאמְרוּ֙ כָּל הָ֣עֵדָ֔ה לִרְגּ֥וֹם אֹתָ֖ם בָּאֲבָנִ֑ים וּכְב֣וֹד יְהוָ֗ה נִרְאָה֙ בְּאֹ֣הֶל מוֹעֵ֔ד אֶֽל כָּל בְּנֵ֖י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל

verses.restored: YHWH said to Moses, How long will this people despise me, and how long will they not trust me, despite all signs I have done in their midst?

familiar.text: And the LORD said unto Moses, How long will this people provoke me? and how long will it be ere they believe me, for all the signs which I have shewed among them?

modern.text: And the LORD said to Moses, “How long will this people treat Me with contempt? How long will they refuse to believe in Me, despite all the signs I have performed among them?

original.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יְהוָה֙ אֶל מֹשֶׁ֔ה עַד אָ֥נָה יְנַאֲצֻ֖נִי הָעָ֣ם הַזֶּ֑ה וְעַד אָ֨נָה֙ לֹא יַאֲמִ֣ינוּ בִ֔י בְּכֹל֙ הָֽאֹת֔וֹת אֲשֶׁ֥ר עָשִׂ֖יתִי בְּקִרְבּֽוֹ

verses.restored: I will strike them with pestilence and dispossess them, and I will make you into a nation greater and mightier than they.

familiar.text: I will smite them with the pestilence, and disinherit them, and will make of thee a greater nation and mightier than they.

modern.text: I will strike them with a plague and destroy them—and I will make you into a nation greater and mightier than they are.” Moses Intercedes for Israel

original.text: אַכֶּ֥נּוּ בַדֶּ֖בֶר וְאוֹרִשֶׁ֑נּוּ וְאֶֽעֱשֶׂה֙ אֹֽתְךָ֔ לְגוֹי גָּד֥וֹל וְעָצ֖וּם מִמֶּֽנּוּ

verses.restored: Moses said to YHWH, Then Egypt will hear, for by your power you brought this people up from its midst,

familiar.text: And Moses said unto the LORD, Then the Egyptians shall hear it, (for thou broughtest up this people in thy might from among them;)

modern.text: But Moses said to the LORD, “The Egyptians will hear of it, for by Your strength You brought this people from among them.

original.text: וַיֹּ֥אמֶר מֹשֶׁ֖ה אֶל יְהוָ֑ה וְשָׁמְע֣וּ מִצְרַ֔יִם כִּֽי הֶעֱלִ֧יתָ בְכֹחֲךָ֛ אֶת הָעָ֥ם הַזֶּ֖ה מִקִּרְבּֽוֹ

verses.restored: and they will tell inhabitant of this land. They have heard that you, YHWH, are in midst of this people, that eye to eye you are seen, YHWH, and your cloud stands over them, and in pillar of cloud you go before them by day and in pillar of fire by night.

familiar.text: And they will tell it to the inhabitants of this land: for they have heard that thou LORD art among this people, that thou LORD art seen face to face, and that thy cloud standeth over them, and that thou goest before them, by day time in a pillar of a cloud, and in a pillar of fire by night.

modern.text: And they will tell it to the inhabitants of this land. They have already heard that You, O LORD, are in the midst of this people, that You, O LORD, have been seen face to face, that Your cloud stands over them, and that You go before them in a pillar of cloud by day and a pillar of fire by night.

verses.restored: If you put this people to death as one man, then nations who have heard your report will say,

familiar.text: Now if thou shalt kill all this people as one man, then the nations which have heard the fame of thee will speak, saying,

modern.text: If You kill this people as one man, the nations who have heard of Your fame will say,

original.text: וְהֵמַתָּ֛ה אֶת הָעָ֥ם הַזֶּ֖ה כְּאִ֣ישׁ אֶחָ֑ד וְאָֽמְרוּ֙ הַגּוֹיִ֔ם אֲשֶׁר שָׁמְע֥וּ אֶֽת שִׁמְעֲךָ֖ לֵאמֹֽר

familiar.text: Because the LORD was not able to bring this people into the land which he sware unto them, therefore he hath slain them in the wilderness.

modern.text: ‘Because the LORD was unable to bring this people into the land He swore to give them, He has slaughtered them in the wilderness.’

original.text: מִבִּלְתִּ֞י יְכֹ֣לֶת יְהוָ֗ה לְהָבִיא֙ אֶת הָעָ֣ם הַזֶּ֔ה אֶל הָאָ֖רֶץ אֲשֶׁר נִשְׁבַּ֣ע לָהֶ֑ם וַיִּשְׁחָטֵ֖ם בַּמִּדְבָּֽר

modern.text: So now I pray, may the power of my Lord be magnified, just as You have declared:

original.text: וְעַתָּ֕ה יִגְדַּל נָ֖א כֹּ֣חַ אֲדֹנָ֑י כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר דִּבַּ֖רְתָּ לֵאמֹֽר

verses.restored: YHWH, slow to anger and great in covenant-love, bearing iniquity and transgression, yet surely not clearing, visiting iniquity of fathers upon children to third and fourth generation.

familiar.text: The LORD is longsuffering, and of great mercy, forgiving iniquity and transgression, and by no means clearing the guilty, visiting the iniquity of the fathers upon the children unto the third and fourth generation.

modern.text: ‘The LORD is slow to anger and abounding in loving devotion, forgiving iniquity and transgression. Yet He will by no means leave the guilty unpunished; He will visit the iniquity of the fathers upon their children to the third and fourth generation.’

verses.restored: Pardon, please, iniquity of this people according to greatness of your covenant-love, and as you have borne this people from Egypt until now.

familiar.text: Pardon, I beseech thee, the iniquity of this people according unto the greatness of thy mercy, and as thou hast forgiven this people, from Egypt even until now.

modern.text: Pardon, I pray, the iniquity of this people, in keeping with the greatness of Your loving devotion, just as You have forgiven them ever since they left Egypt.” God’s Forgiveness and Judgment (Deuteronomy 1:34–40)

verses.restored: YHWH said, I have pardoned according to your word.

familiar.text: And the LORD said, I have pardoned according to thy word:

modern.text: “I have pardoned them as you requested,” the LORD replied.

original.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר יְהוָ֔ה סָלַ֖חְתִּי כִּדְבָרֶֽךָ

verses.restored: But truly, as I live, all earth shall be filled with glory of YHWH.

familiar.text: But as truly as I live, all the earth shall be filled with the glory of the LORD.

modern.text: “Yet as surely as I live and as surely as the whole earth is filled with the glory of the LORD,

original.text: וְאוּלָ֖ם חַי אָ֑נִי וְיִמָּלֵ֥א כְבוֹד יְהוָ֖ה אֶת כָּל הָאָֽרֶץ

verses.restored: For all men who saw my glory and signs that I did in Egypt and in wilderness, yet tested me these ten times and did not listen to my voice,

familiar.text: Because all those men which have seen my glory, and my miracles, which I did in Egypt and in the wilderness, and have tempted me now these ten times, and have not hearkened to my voice;

modern.text: not one of the men who have seen My glory and the signs I performed in Egypt and in the wilderness—yet have tested Me and disobeyed Me these ten times—

verses.restored: surely they shall not see land I swore to their fathers; all who despised me shall not see it.

familiar.text: Surely they shall not see the land which I sware unto their fathers, neither shall any of them that provoked me see it:

modern.text: not one will ever see the land that I swore to give their fathers. None of those who have treated Me with contempt will see it.

original.text: אִם יִרְאוּ֙ אֶת הָאָ֔רֶץ אֲשֶׁ֥ר נִשְׁבַּ֖עְתִּי לַאֲבֹתָ֑ם וְכָל מְנַאֲצַ֖י לֹ֥א יִרְאֽוּהָ

verses.restored: But my servant Caleb, because another spirit was with him and he followed fully after me, I will bring him into land where he went, and his seed shall possess it.

familiar.text: But my servant Caleb, because he had another spirit with him, and hath followed me fully, him will I bring into the land whereinto he went; and his seed shall possess it.

modern.text: But because My servant Caleb has a different spirit and has followed Me wholeheartedly, I will bring him into the land he has entered, and his descendants will inherit it.

original.text: וְעַבְדִּ֣י כָלֵ֗ב עֵ֣קֶב הָֽיְתָ֞ה ר֤וּחַ אַחֶ֨רֶת֙ עִמּ֔וֹ וַיְמַלֵּ֖א אַחֲרָ֑י וַהֲבִֽיאֹתִ֗יו אֶל הָאָ֨רֶץ֙ אֲשֶׁר בָּ֣א שָׁ֔מָּה וְזַרְע֖וֹ יוֹרִשֶֽׁנָּה

familiar.text: Say unto them, As truly as I live, saith the LORD, as ye have spoken in mine ears, so will I do to you:

modern.text: So tell them: As surely as I live, declares the LORD, I will do to you exactly as I heard you say.

original.text: אֱמֹ֣ר אֲלֵהֶ֗ם חַי אָ֨נִי֙ נְאֻם יְהוָ֔ה אִם לֹ֕א כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר דִּבַּרְתֶּ֖ם בְּאָזְנָ֑י כֵּ֖ן אֶֽעֱשֶׂ֥ה לָכֶֽם

verses.restored: In this wilderness your corpses shall fall, all counted of you according to all your number, from twenty years old and upward, who murmured against me.

familiar.text: Your carcases shall fall in this wilderness; and all that were numbered of you, according to your whole number, from twenty years old and upward, which have murmured against me,

modern.text: Your bodies will fall in this wilderness—all who were numbered in the census, everyone twenty years of age or older—because you have grumbled against Me.

original.text: בַּמִּדְבָּ֣ר הַ֠זֶּה יִפְּל֨וּ פִגְרֵיכֶ֜ם וְכָל פְּקֻדֵיכֶם֙ לְכָל מִסְפַּרְכֶ֔ם מִבֶּ֛ן עֶשְׂרִ֥ים שָׁנָ֖ה וָמָ֑עְלָה אֲשֶׁ֥ר הֲלִֽינֹתֶ֖ם עָלָֽי

verses.restored: Surely you shall not enter land concerning which I lifted my hand to settle you in it, except Caleb son of Jephunneh and Joshua son of Nun.

familiar.text: Doubtless ye shall not come into the land, concerning which I sware to make you dwell therein, save Caleb the son of Jephunneh, and Joshua the son of Nun.

modern.text: Surely none of you will enter the land in which I swore to settle you, except Caleb son of Jephunneh and Joshua son of Nun.

original.text: אִם אַתֶּם֙ תָּבֹ֣אוּ אֶל הָאָ֔רֶץ אֲשֶׁ֤ר נָשָׂ֨אתִי֙ אֶת יָדִ֔י לְשַׁכֵּ֥ן אֶתְכֶ֖ם בָּ֑הּ כִּ֚י אִם כָּלֵ֣ב בֶּן יְפֻנֶּ֔ה וִיהוֹשֻׁ֖עַ בִּן נֽוּן

verses.restored: But your little ones, whom you said would become plunder, I will bring them in, and they shall know land that you rejected.

familiar.text: But your little ones, which ye said should be a prey, them will I bring in, and they shall know the land which ye have despised.

modern.text: But I will bring your children, whom you said would become plunder, into the land you have rejected—and they will enjoy it.

original.text: וְטַ֨פְּכֶ֔ם אֲשֶׁ֥ר אֲמַרְתֶּ֖ם לָבַ֣ז יִהְיֶ֑ה וְהֵבֵיאתִ֣י אֹתָ֔ם וְיָֽדְעוּ֙ אֶת הָאָ֔רֶץ אֲשֶׁ֥ר מְאַסְתֶּ֖ם בָּֽהּ

verses.restored: But you, your corpses shall fall in this wilderness.

familiar.text: But as for you, your carcases, they shall fall in this wilderness.

modern.text: As for you, however, your bodies will fall in this wilderness.

original.text: וּפִגְרֵיכֶ֖ם אַתֶּ֑ם יִפְּל֖וּ בַּמִּדְבָּ֥ר הַזֶּֽה

verses.restored: Your children shall be shepherds in wilderness forty years and shall bear your faithlessnesses until your corpses are finished in wilderness.

familiar.text: And your children shall wander in the wilderness forty years, and bear your whoredoms, until your carcases be wasted in the wilderness.

modern.text: Your children will be shepherds in the wilderness for forty years, and they will suffer for your unfaithfulness until the last of your bodies lies in the wilderness.

original.text: וּ֠בְנֵיכֶם יִהְי֨וּ רֹעִ֤ים בַּמִּדְבָּר֙ אַרְבָּעִ֣ים שָׁנָ֔ה וְנָשְׂא֖וּ אֶת זְנוּתֵיכֶ֑ם עַד תֹּ֥ם פִּגְרֵיכֶ֖ם בַּמִּדְבָּֽר

verses.restored: According to number of days that you scouted land, forty days, a day for a year, a day for a year, you shall bear your iniquities forty years and know my opposition.

familiar.text: After the number of the days in which ye searched the land, even forty days, each day for a year, shall ye bear your iniquities, even forty years, and ye shall know my breach of promise.

modern.text: In keeping with the forty days you spied out the land, you shall bear your guilt forty years—a year for each day—and you will experience My alienation.

original.text: בְּמִסְפַּ֨ר הַיָּמִ֜ים אֲשֶׁר תַּרְתֶּ֣ם אֶת הָאָרֶץ֮ אַרְבָּעִ֣ים יוֹם֒ י֣וֹם לַשָּׁנָ֞ה י֣וֹם לַשָּׁנָ֗ה תִּשְׂאוּ֙ אֶת עֲוֺנֹ֣תֵיכֶ֔ם אַרְבָּעִ֖ים שָׁנָ֑ה וִֽידַעְתֶּ֖ם אֶת תְּנוּאָתִֽי

verses.restored: I, YHWH, have spoken. Surely this I will do to all this evil congregation gathered against me: in this wilderness they shall come to an end, and there they shall die.

familiar.text: I the LORD have said, I will surely do it unto all this evil congregation, that are gathered together against me: in this wilderness they shall be consumed, and there they shall die.

modern.text: I, the LORD, have spoken, and I will surely do these things to this entire wicked congregation, which has conspired against Me. They will meet their end in the wilderness, and there they will die.” The Plague on the Ten Spies

original.text: אֲנִ֣י יְהוָה֮ דִּבַּרְתִּי֒ אִם לֹ֣א זֹ֣את אֶֽעֱשֶׂ֗ה לְכָל הָעֵדָ֤ה הָֽרָעָה֙ הַזֹּ֔את הַנּוֹעָדִ֖ים עָלָ֑י בַּמִּדְבָּ֥ר הַזֶּ֛ה יִתַּ֖מּוּ וְשָׁ֥ם יָמֻֽתוּ

verses.restored: The men whom Moses sent to scout land, who returned and made all congregation murmur against him by bringing out evil report against land,

familiar.text: And the men, which Moses sent to search the land, who returned, and made all the congregation to murmur against him, by bringing up a slander upon the land,

modern.text: So the men Moses had sent to spy out the land, who had returned and made the whole congregation grumble against him by bringing out a bad report about the land—

original.text: וְהָ֣אֲנָשִׁ֔ים אֲשֶׁר שָׁלַ֥ח מֹשֶׁ֖ה לָת֣וּר אֶת הָאָ֑רֶץ וַיָּשֻׁ֗בוּ וילונו עָלָיו֙ אֶת כָּל הָ֣עֵדָ֔ה לְהוֹצִ֥יא דִבָּ֖ה עַל הָאָֽרֶץ

verses.restored: those men who brought out evil report of land died by plague before YHWH.

familiar.text: Even those men that did bring up the evil report upon the land, died by the plague before the LORD.

modern.text: those men who had brought out the bad report about the land—were struck down by a plague before the LORD.

original.text: וַיָּמֻ֨תוּ֙ הָֽאֲנָשִׁ֔ים מוֹצִאֵ֥י דִבַּת הָאָ֖רֶץ רָעָ֑ה בַּמַּגֵּפָ֖ה לִפְנֵ֥י יְהוָֽה

verses.restored: But Joshua son of Nun and Caleb son of Jephunneh lived from those men who went to scout land.

familiar.text: But Joshua the son of Nun, and Caleb the son of Jephunneh, which were of the men that went to search the land, lived still.

modern.text: Of those men who had gone to spy out the land, only Joshua son of Nun and Caleb son of Jephunneh remained alive.

original.text: וִיהוֹשֻׁ֣עַ בִּן נ֔וּן וְכָלֵ֖ב בֶּן יְפֻנֶּ֑ה חָיוּ֙ מִן הָאֲנָשִׁ֣ים הָהֵ֔ם הַֽהֹלְכִ֖ים לָת֥וּר אֶת הָאָֽרֶץ

verses.restored: Moses spoke these words to all children of Israel, and people mourned greatly.

familiar.text: And Moses told these sayings unto all the children of Israel: and the people mourned greatly.

modern.text: And when Moses relayed these words to all the Israelites, the people mourned bitterly. The Defeat at Hormah (Deuteronomy 1:41–46)

original.text: וַיְדַבֵּ֤ר מֹשֶׁה֙ אֶת הַדְּבָרִ֣ים הָאֵ֔לֶּה אֶֽל כָּל בְּנֵ֖י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וַיִּֽתְאַבְּל֥וּ הָעָ֖ם מְאֹֽד

verses.restored: They rose early in morning and went up toward top of mountain, saying, Look, we are here, and we will go up to place of which YHWH spoke, for we have sinned/misaligned.

familiar.text: And they rose up early in the morning, and gat them up into the top of the mountain, saying, Lo, we be here, and will go up unto the place which the LORD hath promised: for we have sinned.

modern.text: Early the next morning they got up and went up toward the ridge of the hill country. “We have indeed sinned,” they said, “but we will go to the place the LORD has promised.”

original.text: וַיַּשְׁכִּ֣מוּ בַבֹּ֔קֶר וַיַּֽעֲל֥וּ אֶל רֹאשׁ הָהָ֖ר לֵאמֹ֑ר הִנֶּ֗נּוּ וְעָלִ֛ינוּ אֶל הַמָּק֛וֹם אֲשֶׁר אָמַ֥ר יְהוָ֖ה כִּ֥י חָטָֽאנוּ

verses.restored: Moses said, Why are you crossing mouth/command of YHWH? It will not succeed.

familiar.text: And Moses said, Wherefore now do ye transgress the commandment of the LORD? but it shall not prosper.

modern.text: But Moses said, “Why are you transgressing the commandment of the LORD? This will not succeed!

original.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר מֹשֶׁ֔ה לָ֥מָּה זֶּ֛ה אַתֶּ֥ם עֹבְרִ֖ים אֶת פִּ֣י יְהוָ֑ה וְהִ֖וא לֹ֥א תִצְלָֽח

verses.restored: Do not go up, for YHWH is not in your midst, and do not be struck before your enemies.

familiar.text: Go not up, for the LORD is not among you; that ye be not smitten before your enemies.

modern.text: Do not go up, lest you be struck down by your enemies, because the LORD is not among you.

original.text: אַֽל תַּעֲל֔וּ כִּ֛י אֵ֥ין יְהוָ֖ה בְּקִרְבְּכֶ֑ם וְלֹא֙ תִּנָּ֣גְפ֔וּ לִפְנֵ֖י אֹיְבֵיכֶֽם

verses.restored: For Amalekite and Canaanite are there before you, and you shall fall by sword; because you turned back from after YHWH, YHWH will not be with you.

familiar.text: For the Amalekites and the Canaanites are there before you, and ye shall fall by the sword: because ye are turned away from the LORD, therefore the LORD will not be with you.

modern.text: For there the Amalekites and Canaanites will face you, and you will fall by the sword. Because you have turned away from the LORD, He will not be with you.”

original.text: כִּי֩ הָעֲמָלֵקִ֨י וְהַכְּנַעֲנִ֥י שָׁם֙ לִפְנֵיכֶ֔ם וּנְפַלְתֶּ֖ם בֶּחָ֑רֶב כִּֽי עַל כֵּ֤ן שַׁבְתֶּם֙ מֵאַחֲרֵ֣י יְהוָ֔ה וְלֹא יִהְיֶ֥ה יְהוָ֖ה עִמָּכֶֽם

verses.restored: But they presumed to go up toward top of mountain; ark of covenant of YHWH and Moses did not move from midst of camp.

familiar.text: But they presumed to go up unto the hill top: nevertheless the ark of the covenant of the LORD, and Moses, departed not out of the camp.

modern.text: But they dared to go up to the ridge of the hill country, though neither Moses nor the ark of the covenant of the LORD moved from the camp.

original.text: וַיַּעְפִּ֕לוּ לַעֲל֖וֹת אֶל רֹ֣אשׁ הָהָ֑ר וַאֲר֤וֹן בְּרִית יְהוָה֙ וּמֹשֶׁ֔ה לֹא מָ֖שׁוּ מִקֶּ֥רֶב הַֽמַּחֲנֶֽה

verses.restored: Then Amalekite and Canaanite dwelling in that mountain came down and struck them and beat them down as far as Hormah.

familiar.text: Then the Amalekites came down, and the Canaanites which dwelt in that hill, and smote them, and discomfited them, even unto Hormah.

modern.text: Then the Amalekites and Canaanites who lived in that part of the hill country came down, attacked them, and routed them all the way to Hormah.

original.text: וַיֵּ֤רֶד הָעֲמָלֵקִי֙ וְהַֽכְּנַעֲנִ֔י הַיֹּשֵׁ֖ב בָּהָ֣ר הַה֑וּא וַיַּכּ֥וּם וַֽיַּכְּת֖וּם עַד הַֽחָרְמָֽה

translation_notes: The people's panic reflects trauma, fear for families, and memory of Egypt; it should not be mocked as simple cowardice.
The proposal to return to Egypt shows how oppression can become idealized under fear, but this must not be used to shame trauma responses.
Moses argues with YHWH and appeals to covenant-love, reputation, and prior mercy; intercession is portrayed as legitimate covenant speech, not disobedience.
Verse 20 says pardon is granted, yet severe generational consequences remain. This tension requires theological and trauma-informed audit.
The conquest setting remains ancient and must not justify modern territorial claims, ethnic cleansing, or invasion.
The failed invasion in verses 40-45 shows that confession without listening can become presumptuous violence; remorse does not authorize attack.
The children are not morally blamed for their parents, though they bear consequences of the prior generation's failure.
safety_note: Do not use Numbers 14 to tell traumatized, fearful, displaced, or grieving people that hesitation deserves death, or to justify conquest and war. The chapter preserves severe communal judgment while also modeling intercession, pardon, mourning, and the danger of launching violence after Divine refusal.
